evidenceClasses: CODE < MOCK < BROWSER < PREVIEW < PHYSICAL_DEVICE < PRODUCTION

claims.claim: Canonical iOS container guard: two isolated jars do not share storage; an iOS Safari tab BLOCKS import with Home-Screen-icon guidance (container-guard-banner, class SAFARI_BROWSER); the canonical installed PWA shows no guard and its import persists across reopen. Classification + mutation cases (wrong-container import allowed / browser falsely canonical / 'not configured' for mismatch / container id ignored / stable-host bypass) are unit-proven.
claims.codePath: iosContainer.detectEnvironment -> classifyContainer -> isImportBlockedForContainer; ContactManagement guard banner + save-handler block + recordSaveContainer; familyQuickFaces focusedMissingMessage
claims.mode: Playwright, iPhone UA + navigator.standalone override, deployed canonical origin (guard engages only on canonical host)
claims.limitation: PREVIEW. A fresh isolated jar cannot see another jar; a never-saved PWA is indistinguishable from a first run (honest limit, not overclaimed). The physical confirmation is a single Home-Screen-icon reopen + container receipt.

claims.claim: FORENSIC first-transition analysis: instrumenting the full import->commit->terminate->reopen lifecycle and reading localStorage AND IndexedDB DIRECTLY (independent of the app) at every boundary, there is NO phones>0->0 transition in any channel. The numbers DO become durable: IndexedDB held 3 phones at the UI-success boundary (post durable.flush()) AND at the pre-init reopen boundary (before any app code ran). Therefore the device N->0 is NOT a function/transaction/commit in this code path — it is out-of-process (iOS standalone-PWA/Safari storage partition or ITP eviction).
claims.codePath: ledger B0 seed(0/0) -> B1 validate(0/0) -> B3 UI-success post-flush(ls=3,idb=3) -> B4 Board(3/3) -> TERMINATE -> B5 reopen pre-init(ls=3,idb=3) -> B6 post-init(3/3) -> B7 Board(3/3); firstDrop=null in authoritative/localStorage/indexedDB/resolver
claims.mode: chromium persistent profile, direct localStorage + IndexedDB reads (indexedDB.databases() to avoid probe-created shells), local build of the tested commit
claims.limitation: A single persistent profile is ONE storage partition; it cannot reproduce the iOS cross-partition (PWA vs Safari) read, which is the only remaining device-only hypothesis. Forensic caution recorded: a naive IndexedDB open(name) CREATES an empty DB and masks the real one — the probe uses databases() first.
